questions.stem: What does the gradient of a distance-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: Gradient is the vertical change divided by the horizontal change, which here is distance over time — speed. A horizontal section means stopped.

questions.stem: What is the average rate of change between two points on a curve?
options: The difference between the two y values
The area under the curve between them
The gradient of the straight line joining them
The gradient of the tangent at the first point
questions.explanation: The line joining two points on a curve is a chord, and its gradient is the average rate of change across that interval.

questions.stem: An object falls so that distance is d = 5t². What is its average speed over the first 2 seconds?
questions.explanation: At t = 0, d = 0; at t = 2, d = 20. Average speed is 20 ÷ 2 = 10 m/s. This is not the speed at any particular instant.

questions.stem: What is the instantaneous rate of change at a point on a curve?
options: The value of y at that point
The gradient of the tangent at that point
The gradient of a chord through that point
The average of the gradients either side of it
questions.explanation: As the second point slides closer, the chord approaches the tangent, and the tangent gradient is the rate at that exact instant. This idea becomes differentiation.

questions.stem: How can an instantaneous rate of change be estimated from a graph?
options: Measure the area beneath the curve
Draw a tangent at the point and find its gradient
Read off the y value at that point
Find the gradient between the two endpoints
questions.explanation: Drawing the tangent by eye and taking rise over run is the standard method, and the accuracy depends entirely on how well the tangent is drawn.

questions.stem: A speed-time graph is a straight line rising from the origin. What does this show?
questions.explanation: On a speed-time graph the gradient is the acceleration, so a constant gradient means constant acceleration. A horizontal line would mean constant speed.

questions.stem: On a speed-time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
questions.explanation: Speed multiplied by time gives distance, and that product is exactly the area beneath the graph. This is why area matters on one graph and not on the other.

questions.stem: Which relationship shows y in direct proportion to x?
questions.explanation: Direct proportion means y is a constant multiple of x, so the graph is a straight line through the origin. Adding a constant breaks it, because the line no longer passes through zero.

questions.stem: In direct variation y = kx, what does k represent?
options: The value of y when x equals zero
questions.explanation: k is the fixed ratio y ÷ x, and it is also the gradient of the line. Finding k from one pair of values is the first step in nearly every variation question.

questions.stem: If y varies directly with x and y = 12 when x = 3, find y when x = 7.
questions.explanation: Find k = 12 ÷ 3 = 4, so y = 4x, and at x = 7 that gives 28. Always find k explicitly rather than adding on, which works only by coincidence.

questions.stem: What does inverse variation mean?
options: One quantity is the negative of the other
The graph is a straight line
As one quantity doubles, the other halves
questions.explanation: In inverse variation the product is constant: xy = k, so y = k/x. The graph is a hyperbola rather than a line.

questions.stem: Six workers take 10 days to finish a job. Assuming inverse variation, how long would 4 workers take?
questions.explanation: The product is constant: 6 × 10 = 60 worker-days, so 60 ÷ 4 = 15 days. Fewer workers means more time, which checks that the answer is on the right side of the original.

questions.stem: The graph of y = k/x has which feature?
options: It crosses the y-axis at k
It is a straight line through the origin
It has a minimum turning point
It approaches both axes without touching them
questions.explanation: The axes are asymptotes: x can never be zero and y never reaches zero. That is what distinguishes this shape from every other graph in the course.

questions.stem: A car covers 60 km at 60 km/h and the next 60 km at 30 km/h. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance over total time: 120 km in 1 + 2 = 3 hours, giving 40 km/h. Averaging the two speeds gives 45 and is wrong, because more time was spent at the slower speed.

questions.stem: How does the rate of change behave for a quantity growing exponentially?
options: It increases as the quantity increases
questions.explanation: Exponential growth multiplies by a constant factor each period, so the amount added each period gets larger. That is why the curve steepens, unlike a straight line.

questions.stem: For h = 20t − 5t², what is the average rate of change of height from t = 0 to t = 2?
questions.explanation: At t = 0, h = 0; at t = 2, h = 20. The average rate is 20 ÷ 2 = 10 m/s upward. At t = 2 itself the object is at its highest point and the instantaneous rate is zero, which is why the two differ.

questions.stem: Water drains from a tank so the depth falls quickly at first and then more slowly. What shape is the graph?
options: A curve that starts flat and then steepens
A curve that is steep at first and then flattens
questions.explanation: A falling rate of change shows as a curve whose gradient becomes less steep. A straight line would mean the depth fell by the same amount every minute.

questions.stem: Two quantities are in direct proportion. Which point must the graph pass through?
options: A point on the y-axis above zero
questions.explanation: If y = kx then x = 0 gives y = 0, so the line must pass through (0, 0). A line that does not is linear but not proportional.

questions.stem: A rate of change is negative. What does that tell you?
options: The graph lies below the x-axis
The rate has been calculated wrongly
questions.explanation: A negative gradient means the quantity falls as the variable increases. The quantity itself can be positive the whole time, which is the distinction being tested.

questions.stem: Which of these is a rate?
questions.explanation: A rate compares two quantities with different units. Fuel consumption, speed, price per litre and heart rate are all rates; a single measurement is not.

questions.stem: A car travels 150 km in 2 hours. What is its average speed?
questions.explanation: Average speed is total distance over total time, so 150 ÷ 2. Multiplying instead of dividing gives a figure no road car reaches.

questions.stem: A tap fills a 60 litre tank in 5 minutes. What is the rate in litres per minute?
questions.explanation: Divide the amount by the time: 60 ÷ 5 = 12. The unit tells you which way round to divide, because litres per minute means litres divided by minutes.

questions.stem: Two distance-time lines are drawn, one steeper than the other. What does that mean?
options: The steeper line took more time
The steeper line covered less distance
The steeper line is the faster journey
The steeper line is the longer journey
questions.explanation: Gradient on a distance-time graph is speed, so a steeper line covers more distance in the same time. Steepness says nothing about how far or how long on its own.

questions.stem: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal line mean?
options: The object is moving at a steady speed
questions.explanation: No change in distance over time means no movement. A steady speed would be a sloping straight line instead.

questions.stem: What does the gradient of a speed-time graph represent?
questions.explanation: Gradient is change in speed over change in time, which is acceleration. The area under that graph gives the distance instead.

questions.stem: A car accelerates from rest to 20 m/s over 8 s. How far does it travel?
questions.explanation: The speed-time graph is a triangle, and the area under it is the distance: ½ × 8 × 20 = 80 m. Multiplying 20 by 8 gives 160 m, which would be the distance at a constant 20 m/s rather than while speeding up.

questions.stem: A recipe uses 300 g of flour for 12 biscuits. How much for 20 biscuits?
questions.explanation: Each biscuit needs 25 g, so 20 need 500 g. Finding the unit amount first is the most reliable way through a proportion question.

questions.stem: Which is the better value: 400 g for $6 or 600 g for $8.40?
questions.explanation: The unit prices are $15 and $14 per kilogram, so the larger pack is cheaper per gram. Comparing per unit is the only fair comparison.

questions.stem: A population of 2000 grows by 5% each year. What is it after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 1.05 twice: 2000 × 1.1025 = 2205. Adding 5% of the original twice gives 2200 and misses the growth on the growth.

questions.stem: Why is compound growth larger than simple growth over several periods?
options: It is calculated more often per year
Simple growth ignores the starting amount
Each period grows on the new total, not the original
questions.explanation: Compounding applies the rate to a total that already includes earlier growth. The rate itself stays the same, which is what makes this counterintuitive.

questions.stem: A car worth $30000 depreciates 15% a year. What is it worth after 2 years?
questions.explanation: Multiply by 0.85 twice: 30000 × 0.7225 = 21675. Depreciation is compound in the same way growth is, just with a multiplier below 1.

questions.stem: A shirt is $40 after a 20% discount. What was the original price?
questions.explanation: The sale price is 80% of the original, so divide by 0.8. Adding 20% to $40 gives $48, which is the classic reverse-percentage error.

questions.stem: Convert 72 km/h into metres per second.
questions.explanation: Divide by 3.6 to get 20 m/s. A quick check is that 72 km/h is a highway speed, and 20 m/s covers a footy field in five seconds.

questions.stem: A pipe fills a pool in 6 hours and another in 3 hours. Together, how long do they take?
questions.explanation: Add the rates rather than the times: one sixth plus one third is one half of the pool per hour, so 2 hours. Averaging the times gives 4.5 and is wrong.

questions.stem: A phone plan charges $30 plus $0.20 per GB. What is the cost for 25 GB?
questions.explanation: The variable part is 25 × 0.20 = $5, added to the fixed $30. Flat plus per-unit is the most common rate structure in real bills.

questions.stem: What is a unit rate?
options: A rate written as a percentage
An amount expressed per one of something
The total of two quantities added
questions.explanation: Dividing to get a per-one figure makes different offers directly comparable. Shelf labels in supermarkets do exactly this.

questions.stem: A runner covers 400 m in 50 seconds. What is the pace in seconds per 100 m?
questions.explanation: Divide the time by four, since 400 m is four lots of 100 m. Pace is time per distance, which is the inverse of speed.

questions.stem: A graph shows distance rising steeply then levelling off. What happened?
options: The object moved fast then stopped
The object stopped then moved fast
The object accelerated the whole time
questions.explanation: A steep gradient is a high speed and a flat section is no movement, so the order of the sections gives the order of events. Reading left to right is what tells the story.

questions.stem: What is 15% of 240?
questions.explanation: Ten percent is 24 and five percent is 12, so the total is 36. Splitting a percentage into easy parts is faster than reaching for a calculator.

questions.stem: A quantity rises from 80 to 100. What is the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 20 on an original of 80, so 20 ÷ 80 = 25%. Dividing by the new value instead gives 20%, which is the most common error.

questions.stem: A price rises 10% then falls 10%. What is the net effect?
options: It ends slightly below the original
It ends slightly above the original
questions.explanation: The fall applies to the larger amount, so 1.1 × 0.9 = 0.99, leaving 99% of the original. Percentage changes never simply cancel.

questions.stem: A map scale is 1 cm to 5 km. How far apart are two towns 7 cm apart on the map?
questions.explanation: Multiply by the scale: 7 × 5 = 35 km. A scale is itself a rate, in kilometres per centimetre.
